trials.name: TOGETHER / AH0003
trials.population: Adults aged 50 to 80 years with prodromal/mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild AD, and evidence of cerebral Aβ accumulation.
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline to Week 80 in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) total score
trials.results_summary: Results are not yet posted to the registry, but published abstracts indicate bepranemab slowed tau accumulation by 33-58% versus placebo on tau-PET. Exposure-response modeling of a low-tau/APOE4 non-carrier responder subpopulation suggested a clinical benefit, indicating higher doses might improve clinical outcomes.

trials.name: PSP003
trials.population: Adults aged 40 years and older with possible or probable Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) Richardson's Syndrome.
trials.primary_endpoint: Incidence of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) from Baseline up to Week 68
trials.results_summary: A 2026 published paper reports that the drug demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile alongside biomarker assessments in participants with PSP.

trials.name: PSP002
trials.population: Participants who completed the Treatment Period in the PSP003 (NCT04185415) trial.
trials.primary_endpoint: Incidence of treatment emergent adverse events from Baseline of the open-label extension to the end of the study

trials.name: UP0047
trials.population: Healthy male subjects aged 18 to 75 years.
trials.primary_endpoint: The incidence of Adverse Events (AEs) during the study from Visit 1 up to the Safety Follow-Up Visit
trials.results_summary: Published results from two Phase 1 studies in healthy participants showed the expected safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile for bepranemab.

trials.name: UP0065
trials.population: Healthy Japanese male and female subjects aged 20 to 75 years.
trials.primary_endpoint: The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events during the study from first dose to safety follow-up/withdraw
trials.results_summary: Evaluated safety and PK in healthy Japanese participants; data grouped in a joint Phase 1 publication showing safety and tolerability across ethnicities.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence for bepranemab (UCB0107) is driven primarily by the Phase 2 TOGETHER trial in prodromal to mild Alzheimer's disease, supported by earlier Phase 1 safety data in healthy volunteers and PSP patients. While the full primary clinical endpoint (CDR-SB) results for the overall Phase 2 AD cohort remain unposted, recent abstracts report robust target engagement, with bepranemab slowing tau accumulation by 33-58% versus placebo on tau-PET. Additionally, exposure-response modeling indicates potential clinical benefit within a specific responder subpopulation of low-tau or APOE4 non-carriers. Overall, while biomarker outcomes are promising and confirm the drug's mechanism of action, definitive evidence of broad clinical efficacy in AD awaits full peer-reviewed publication of the Phase 2 primary clinical outcomes.
discrepancies: The input document accurately notes that Phase 2 (NCT04867616) results have not been posted to the registry, but it omits that early biomarker efficacy and clinical modeling results were published as conference abstracts in December 2025 showing tau accumulation slowing and potential subpopulation clinical benefits.
